chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from al-Walid ibn Sabih, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

When you go out for your needs after the obligatory prayer, pray two Rak'at. When you finish the Tashahhud, say: 'O Allah, I have gone out seeking from Your Grace as You commanded me, so provide me with a permissible, goodly sustenance and grant me well-being in what You have provided me.' Repeat this three times.

Then pray two more Rak'at. When you finish the Tashahhud, say: 'By the might and power of Allah, I go out without any might or power from myself, but by Your might, O Lord, and Your power. I disassociate from might and power [in myself] and turn to You. O Allah, I ask You for the blessings of this day and its people, and I ask You to provide me from Your Grace with a broad, goodly, permissible sustenance, which You bring to me by Your might and power, while I am humble in Your well-being.' Say this three times.

key_terms.بِحَوْلِ اللَّهِ وَ قُوَّتِهِ: By the might and power of Allah

ai.seo_question: What are the specific prayers and supplications to recite when going out to seek lawful livelihood?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith details the specific Sunnah of Salat al-Rizq, prescribing two sets of two Rak'at prayers with distinct supplications to seek lawful sustenance after the obligatory prayer. The first supplication focuses on asking for halal provision as commanded by God, while the second emphasizes reliance on divine power (bi-hawlihi wa quwwatihi) and seeks blessings for the day, reflecting the Shia emphasis on combining ritual worship with active supplication for worldly needs.
